clue.text: To relieve tension, hear recital performed

indicators.note: a piece performed is worked through afresh, so these letters are played into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone eases a tense atmosphere by listening to a musical recital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performed' is the anagram signal: HEAR plus RECITAL, eleven letters, rearranged into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear the air is the idiom for dispelling bad feeling or a strained mood.

clue.text: Vehicle left-under cover here?

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
port is the nautical word for the left-hand side

explanation.surface: A car is parked under shelter, the clue asking whether this is the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A carport is an open-sided shelter where a motorist keeps a vehicle covered.

clue.text: An authoritative pronouncement from the dictionary

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: An official ruling is quoted straight out of a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is a formal decree issued by someone in power.

clue.text: Tedious routine? Come down to this county

parts.note: a rut is a dull, unchanging routine
to land is to come down to earth

explanation.surface: Someone bored with life is told to come and settle in a quiet shire.
explanation.walkthrough: RUTLAND is the smallest historic county in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rutland is an English county in the East Midlands, named here by the pointer phrase.

clue.text: When these books are in service, sing praises

definitions.text: When these books are in service, sing praises

parts.words: When these books are in service, sing praises
parts.note: the books brought out during a church service are the ones from which a congregation sings songs of praise

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is told to sing out once the books come out at the service.
explanation.definitionFit: Hymn books are used in worship so the congregation can sing praise together.

clue.text: A tonic did wonders for this craving

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something that did wonders worked a transformation, so these letters are transformed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pick-me-up drink worked so well that the drinker now longs for more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'did wonders' reads as praise of the tonic, but DID is part of the fodder: A, TONIC and DID, nine letters, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An addiction is a compulsive dependence, a craving the sufferer cannot shake off.

clue.text: Like grandpa in chair, or youngster playing music?

definitions.meaning: an old man in a chair that moves to and fro, swaying gently
a young person playing rock music, informally said to be really going for it

explanation.surface: Grandad sways in his chair while the grandchild plays loud music.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses: moving back and forth in a rocking chair, and playing rock music.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocking means swaying to and fro, and also playing or enjoying lively rock music.

clue.text: Keep on being cheeky about little relative

indicators.note: about here means going round, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: pert means saucy or cheeky
sis is a short form of sister, a relative

explanation.surface: A child keeps being rude to a younger sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is only a link; 'about' is the container signal, with the cheeky word wrapped round the little relative.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to carry on doggedly without stopping.

clue.text: Doorman takes home steak

parts.note: a porter guards the door of a building such as a hotel
a house is a home

explanation.surface: A hotel doorkeeper carries a cut of beef back to his lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Porterhouse is a thick cut of beef taken from the short loin.

clue.text: A small quantity of Latin?

parts.note: reads as a scrap of the language, but means a small amount expressed in a word borrowed directly from Latin

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to knowing only a smattering of the classical language.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a small amount and is taken unchanged from Latin, where it meant moderate.

clue.text: Pantomime gets the bird

definitions.meaning: a traditional British Christmas stage show of this title, starring a pantomime dame
a female goose that is a parent, a mother bird

explanation.surface: A Christmas show earns the derisive whistling of the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' suggests a show being booed; it is only a link between two senses. A pantomime is a comic British family stage show performed at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a classic Christmas show and literally describes a goose that has young.

clue.text: Soldiers returned, having no way settled to sleep

definitions.note: the clue gives the past tense, while the answer is the verb or the place where birds rest

indicators.note: returned means the soldiers' abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers
O is nought, nothing
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: Troops come back with nowhere to go and bed down for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds roost when they perch and settle for the night.

clue.text: No government supporter

parts.note: reads as someone who opposes the ruling party, but means a person who backs having no government at all

explanation.surface: A voter is described as opposing those currently in power.
explanation.definitionFit: An anarchist advocates abolishing the state and all rule by authority.

clue.text: Some apprentice disgracefully led astray

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A trainee is shamefully lured into wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enticed is to be tempted or lured away from the right path.

clue.text: Space for tennis? Hold trial here

definitions.meaning: a court for a racket game, plus room to play it
the place where a judge hears a case

explanation.surface: A hall with room for a game of tennis doubles as the place for a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtroom is the chamber where legal cases are tried; whimsically, a room for a court.

clue.text: Perhaps English beach

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word could be otherwise, so its letters may be rearranged

explanation.surface: The clue describes a typical stretch of coast in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' looks like 'for example', but it signals an anagram of ENGLISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is a coast covered in pebbles, a common kind of seashore.

clue.text: About to drink, to interrupt his spasms

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into something, so these letters go in the middle of his

parts.note: taken as written
C, circa, means about
a cup is a drink, as in a fruit cup

explanation.surface: A man about to take a drink is cut short by hiccoughs.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'to' is a link; 'About' gives C as circa, not the container signal, which is 'interrupt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiccups are involuntary spasms of the diaphragm.

clue.text: Plausible arguer makes a Conservative's suit fall apart

indicators.note: a suit that falls apart comes to pieces, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, with the S of the possessive kept
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tory politician's clothing comes to pieces in public.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive's S is a letter here: A, C, S and SUIT rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A casuist reasons cleverly but speciously, especially about moral questions.

clue.text: Trembles and smashes

definitions.meaning: shakes, as from cold or fear
breaks into fragments, as glass does

explanation.surface: Someone quivers and breaks things.
explanation.definitionFit: To shiver is to quake, and also to shatter into slivers.

clue.text: Curse pet with cowed air

parts.note: hang, as in 'hang it all', is a mild curse
a dog is a pet

explanation.surface: Someone swears at a pet that slinks away looking cowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog look is shamefaced and browbeaten.

clue.text: Meal excellent-ate out

parts.note: high means of superior quality, excellent

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone ate a superb meal while dining out.
explanation.definitionFit: High tea is an early-evening cooked meal served with tea, mainly in Britain.

clue.text: Praised for beating depression

indicators.note: a beating knocks something about, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone is praised for having overcome low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is utter hopelessness, a deep low mood.

clue.text: Causing annoyance by clumsiness?

explanation.surface: A clumsy person irritates others by knocking things over.
explanation.definitionFit: Upsetting means distressing, and literally overturning something.

clue.text: Blow oxygen with relish

parts.note: a gust is a blow of wind
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Someone breathes in fresh air with enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment or zest.

clue.text: Big fireplace, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is said aloud and matched with one sounding the same

parts.note: a grate is the frame that holds a fire in a fireplace

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a hearth is huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Great means large or of considerable size.

clue.text: Point to good book, a typical example

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
pi, short for pious, means good
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Someone indicates a fine volume as a model specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect representative instance of a class.

clue.text: Adolescent period be fore one makes a score?

definitions.meaning: the years from thirteen to nineteen

definitions.text: be fore one makes a score?
definitions.meaning: the time before a person reaches twenty, a score being twenty

explanation.surface: Youth is described as the time before achieving anything in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' suggests points in a game; here it is twenty years.
explanation.definitionFit: The teenage years are those of youth before adulthood, ending at twenty.

clue.text: So, man, hatter made you this?

definitions.text: So, man, hatter made you this?

indicators.note: made suggests something put together from materials, so these letters are formed into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A customer is asked whether a milliner produced this headgear for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges SO, MAN and HATTER into the hat a hatter might make.
explanation.definitionFit: A tam-o'-shanter is a Scottish woollen bonnet, the kind of headwear a hatter makes.
